actionsReview.result: All 13 used actions already match the newest stable action release and its verified commit SHA. Annotated tags were resolved to their target commits; CodeQL bundle releases and prereleases were excluded.

python.name: frostwork
python.note: Resolved from the F-UJI dependency tree; already present before this update.

python.name: fuji
python.note: The PyPI package named fuji is unrelated and is not used.

compatibilityChanges: jsdom 31.0.1, Oxfmt 0.78.0 and SoupSieve 4.1.1 are now included instead of being deferred; frontend tests, formatting and offline HTML extraction verify their compatibility.
The npm Playwright 1.65.1 package and its matching Microsoft image are both available; F-UJI independently uses Python Playwright 1.65.2 with its matching Chromium build.
F-UJI installs libatomic1 before invoking the Node runtime bundled with Playwright.
The Minimatch regression expects bounded rejection of excessive glob expansion instead of truncated expansion; normal Swagger file allowlists remain covered.
The local deepmerge security patch remains because upstream deepmerge 4.3.1 does not replace it.

The temporary browser backend uses an unavailable loopback endpoint for the optional legacy citation cache, avoiding delays from unreachable internal DNS; the normal development connection is restored after each run.

Playwright 1.65.1 reproduced ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES on the first stylesheet request in remote Linux Chromium; the existing native TLS preflight for fulfilled HTML now applies to Chromium and WebKit on all host platforms, without relaxing stylesheet assertions or certificate handling.

PHPStan 2.3.6 infers the FAIR score array shapes and bounded ZIP float sums precisely; obsolete type assertions and an unreachable float-infinity check were removed, with 106 existing service tests verifying the behavior.

imageScan.scope: Local linux/amd64 images; OS and language packages; HIGH and CRITICAL findings, including those without available fixes; no new suppressions.

images.name: mysql
images.limitation: The latest official MySQL 9.7.4 image still bundles vulnerable mysqlsh Python libraries and a gosu binary built with an older Go toolchain. Fix versions exist for those components, but no newer supported official 9.7 image was available. The server pin is retained; these findings are not described as fixed or suppressed.

releaseGate.evidence: Evaluated from the complete local scan reports without suppressions; this does not assert a CI run or the absence of unfixed vulnerabilities.

environment.workers: Repository wrappers selected defaults from available CPUs; no parallelism override.

playwrightFocused.command: Critical embargo and landing-page regressions: Chromium, five repetitions each

developmentRestored.notes: HTTP 200 with the documented localhost certificate verification and ERNIE Host routing; normal Compose app/webserver restored, Vite hot file restored, two assessment workers running, and the temporary browser server removed.

validation.artifacts: Raw logs and image scan reports are local ignored artifacts under storage/logs/dependency-update-113; this tracked inventory preserves their results.
validationCorrections: After an initial shared-workspace collision between the backend and MySQL wrappers, the affected PHP test path passed in isolation and the complete backend suite was rerun sequentially.
PHPStan 2.3.6 reported obsolete type assertions and an unreachable float-infinity check; the focused service tests and final complete backend check passed after removing them.

The first browser run found two stale local TEST fixtures and a stylesheet TLS failure. Only the two guarded TEST records were refreshed against the existing seeder, with original values saved in browser-fixtures-before.json.

Repeated browser tests captured ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES on the first stylesheet request in remote Linux Chromium. After extending the existing native TLS preflight to all host platforms, all 20 focused repetitions passed.

The complete browser run subsequently passed 435 cases and found the same XML-import timeout in each browser because the local legacy citation database hostname was unreachable. The temporary backend now exercises its immediate loopback fallback; the import and remaining tombstone cases passed all 15 focused checks across the three browsers; each XML import returned HTTP 200 within the existing timeout.
